summary: The new-generation ES is Lexus Australia's first battery-electric sedan, a large five-seater sold as the front-drive ES350e ($77,000) and dual-motor ES500e ($84,000) Sports Luxury, both on a 74.7kWh pack (about 71kWh usable) shared with the RZ and bZ4X. Australian reviewers rate it highly for ride comfort, refinement, rear legroom and equipment for the money — CarsGuide scored the ES350e 8.1/10 and Chasing Cars the ES500e 8.0 — but split on the cabin, which several find less characterful and more touchscreen-dependent than past Lexus models, and on range, which Chasing Cars calls mediocre at 465-510km WLTP.
pros: Strong value for a luxury EV sedan: the ES350e at $77,000 and ES500e at $84,000 before on-road costs both sit under the $91,661 fuel-efficient LCT threshold, so either qualifies for the FBT exemption on a novated lease bought before April 2027
Efficient for its size: 16.4kWh/100km claimed for the ES350e and 17.9 for the ES500e, and Chasing Cars measured 16.8kWh/100km overall in the heavier ES500e with high-15s around town
22kW three-phase AC charging (10-100% in about 4.5 hours) and 150kW DC (10-80% in about 28 minutes) on both grades
Five-year unlimited-kilometre warranty with no servicing condition, plus a separate eight-year/160,000km drive-battery warranty
Reviewers consistently praise the ride, refinement and vast rear legroom, and both grades come fully loaded with 21-inch wheels, adaptive suspension and a power driver's seat
cons: The rear backrest is fixed, so the 517-litre boot cannot be extended — only a ski port passes long items through, which rules out flat-pack loads a fold-down rival such as the Tesla Model 3 swallows
Not rated to tow (0kg braked), where the RZ SUV on the same platform is rated to 1500kg

Both grades sit above the $75,000 FBT exemption cap that applies from 1 April 2027, and capped-price servicing for the EV is $625 per visit ($3,125 over five years), which CarExpert flags as expensive for an electric car
Range is middling for the money: 510km WLTP for the ES350e and 465km for the ES500e, and CarsGuide's mixed test projected only about 380km from the ES350e

The cabin moves drive modes and climate controls into the touchscreen, a step backwards in CarsGuide's and Chasing Cars' view, the driver-attention monitor is aggressive, and there is no spare wheel, only a repair kit
